title: Assessing Trauma-related Links Between Affective and Metabolic Systems
official: From Hyperarousal to Hyperglycemia: Therapeutic Targeting of Noradrenergic Signaling in PTSD-Related Insulin Resistance
summary:
KEY INFORMATION: The purpose of this study is to understand how insulin resistance (how your body processes sugar) and PTSD might be related. The goal is to improve the health of Veterans in three ways:

1. Understanding health risks: The investigators want to learn why Veterans with post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) are more likely to develop medical problems related to insulin resistance, such as diabetes.
2. Testing effects of a medication: The investigators are testing whether prazosin, a medication that studies have shown may address some PTSD symptoms, can also improve how the body responds to insulin. If it does, this could point to a specific biological pathway that could be targeted for development of new treatments to prevent insulin resistance and diabetes in Veterans with PTSD.
3. Links to depression. The investigators will also look at whether insulin sensitivity affects depression symptoms in people with PTSD. This may inform future research into treatments for PTSD.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

1. Veteran of the US military
2. Diagnosis of post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) defined by Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders (DSM-5) symptom count on Clinician-Administered PTSD Scale for DSM-5 (CAPS-5)

Exclusion Criteria:

1. Any form of diabetes as defined by the American Diabetes Association. Exceptions may be made for participants with previously undiagnosed, early, asymptomatic Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus (T2DM) who meet American Diabetes Association criteria for diabetes during study screening who wish to be included
2. Diagnosis of DSM-5-defined bipolar I, schizophrenia spectrum or other psychotic disorders (by MINI)
3. Diagnosis of dementia or related progressive neurocognitive disorder, based on clinical records
4. Diagnosis of moderate or severe substance use disorder (except for caffeine and nicotine) during the preceding 3 months
5. Current use or use within the past 2 weeks of a medication with significant 1-AR or 2-AR activity (prazosin, doxazosin, alfuzosin, clonidine, guanfacine), or opiates
6. Current use or use within the past 3 months of antipsychotics, glucocorticoid medications, or glucose-lowering medications, including but not limited to metformin and GLP-1 agonists
7. Contraindication to prazosin
8. History of moderate or severe Traumatic Brain Injury (TBI) as defined by the Ohio State University TBI Identification Method
9. Increased risk of suicide that necessitates inpatient treatment, intensive outpatient care, or treatment excluded by the protocol
10. Pregnancy or lactation, or anticipated pregnancy at any point during study participation
11. Ongoing or initiation of new treatment with evidence-based trauma-focused therapy for post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) within 2 weeks of baseline. Supportive psychotherapy may be continued during the study.
12. Current enrollment in another interventional trial for post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD)
